slides.say: Triangle A B C is a right triangle. Given: angle A B C is ninety degrees, A B is five centimeters, and B C is seven centimeters. What is A C, in centimeters?

The same kind of triangle as before, with different numbers. The right angle is at B again, so A C, across from it, is the hypotenuse, and A B and B C are the legs. [short pause] We'll use the Pythagorean theorem.

[short pause] A B squared plus B C squared equals A C squared. Five squared is twenty-five, and seven squared is forty-nine. Twenty-five plus forty-nine is seventy-four. So A C squared is seventy-four.
at: A B squared plus B C squared

slides.say: Last time we got a round number. Here we don't, and that's completely fine. We take the root of both sides. The root undoes the square, so A C is the square root of seventy-four. We leave it exactly like that. Choice number one is our answer.
at: so A C is the square root
Choice number one is our answer

slides.say: A quick sense check. Eight squared is sixty-four and nine squared is eighty-one, so the root of seventy-four is between eight and nine. That's longer than each leg, as a hypotenuse should be, and shorter than five plus seven.

The other choices are common mistakes. Twelve adds the lengths, not the squares. Seventy-four forgets the root. And the root of twenty-four subtracts the squares, as if we were looking for a leg. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
